hook: The last great ruler of the Aztecs, who welcomed Cortés into his city.

pages.x: Moctezuma was born around 1466, a nephew of earlier Aztec rulers. He served as a priest and a successful general, and in 1502 was chosen huey tlatoani, "great speaker", the ruler of the Aztec Empire.

He ruled from Tenochtitlan, a city of perhaps 200,000 people on an island in a lake, bigger than any city in Spain, with causeways, canals, floating gardens and the Great Temple at its heart. He was carried in a litter, and commoners had to look at the ground as he passed.
Runners brought him fresh fish from the coast, hundreds of kilometres away. The Spanish wrote that he drank frothy chocolate from golden cups, and at each meal chose from hundreds of dishes.

Later accounts said omens had warned of disaster: a comet, a temple bursting into flames, a woman weeping in the night for her children. Whether he really believed the Spanish leader was the returning god Quetzalcoatl is doubted by historians today.
In November 1519 he met Hernán Cortés on the causeway into the city, welcomed him as a guest and lodged the Spaniards in a palace. Days later, Cortés took him prisoner in his own city.

In 1520, after the Spaniards massacred Aztec nobles at a festival, the city rose up. Moctezuma was brought out to calm the crowd and was struck by stones. Whether he died of those wounds or was killed by the Spaniards is still argued.
Moctezuma ruled the Aztec Empire at its height, and saw it fall to a few hundred Spaniards and their many native allies. His name lives on as the symbol of the last days of the Aztecs.
pts: Ruled the Aztec Empire at its height
Lord of Tenochtitlan, one of the world's largest cities
His capture began the fall of the Aztecs
